rulings.evidence: Light mayo is the same jar on the same shelf at the same price class, per the 'Light Cream Cheese' and 'avocado oil mayonnaise' precedents; same gram weight per cup. Only the macros differ, so it gets its own DB row rather than its own commodity.

rulings.raw: 1 Tbsp. powdered peanut butter, PB2 (13g (see notes))
rulings.evidence: REFUSED both near matches: the board's `butter` is dairy butter (wrong food) and `peanut-butter` is the jarred spread at roughly a fifth the price per ounce with 590 vs 400 cal/100 g. Pantry-static rather than a new specialty id for a 13 g flavour line; term reported absent so the pricing road can rule.

You buy the dry bag and cook it: `rice` is the same product and price class, and 'cooked' is a prep instruction as in the 'cooked bacon' ruling. Weighed cooked (158 g/cup) so grams and the cooked-rice DB row agree; vocabulary wants a Cooked White Rice name row, not a new id.

REFUSED the board's `rice` match outright - cauliflower is not rice, that is a wrong-food match at a wrong price. Also refused fresh `cauliflower`: fresh-is-not-frozen is a standing rejection and a bagged frozen riced product is a different price class. New id proposed.

Shredding is a knife cut of the same head, per the 'carrot' -> carrots precedent; not a bagged coleslaw mix at this quantity. Board 6 of 7. Unquantified topping weighed at about 1/2 cup shredded per bowl.

Quick-pickled at home from a whole onion plus pantry vinegar, so both the purchase and the macros are the onion; canon reuses the existing Yellow Onion row. Unquantified garnish with no stated quantity, hence optional, per the 'Sliced onions' precedent.

Brand-specific jarred candied jalapeno with no stated quantity, named in the ingredient list but in no instruction step; dropped on the 'avocado lime dipping sauce' precedent. REFUSED the board's `jalapenos` match: that is fresh peppers, a form flip and a different price class.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: A bagged frozen riced-cauliflower product, 1,190 g at batch scale, so a material purchase and not a garnish. Nothing on the pre-resolve table prices it: the board's only offer was `rice` (a different food) and the near vocabulary rows were all rice. It is NOT the live `cauliflower` id - that is a fresh head, and fresh-is-not-frozen is a standing estate rejection with a different price per pound and a different gram yield. The estate already mints frozen-vegetable ids separately from their fresh twins: `frozen-broccoli-florets` is used by another recipe in this very batch. If an id already prices bagged frozen riced cauliflower under another spelling (frozen-riced-cauliflower, cauliflower-rice), alias it and I withdraw.
